look_here_first: LEAVES FIRST, BUT THE SEEDS FINISH THE ID. Euphorbia simulans is a low, largely glabrous desert sandmat with very short opposing ROUND to oval entire leaves (1–3.2 mm long) with near-symmetric bases. The small red-purple cyathial glands are ELLIPTIC and lack the white crescents of E. golondrina; Nathan Taylor's licensed true gland photograph now shows their shape. The smooth green THREE-LOBED capsule is photographed too. The decisive look-alike E. theriaca can look almost identical above ground: true SIMULANS SEEDS are generally 1.5–2 mm with 5–7 WEAK interrupted transverse wrinkles or pits, while THERIACA has smaller seeds with usually 2–4 MUCH DEEPER clear grooves. Both real seed macro photographs and author-stated 0.5mm calibration are now in the genus comparison. Still missing: independently measured same-node 0.5–0.7 mm stipules. FNA records simulans in Brewster, Hudspeth and Presidio; NOT validated as native to Hays or a local crew weed.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite usually unequal leaves, cyathia rather than ordinary flowers, and 3-lobed capsule that dries and releases seeds.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual or short-lived perennial; usually slender taproot/rootstock; prostrate to reclining glabrous branches about 5–40 cm, growing in arid desert scrub and rocky or sandy ground.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, ORBICULATE, OVAL or very short oblong, 1–3.2 × 1.5–5 mm; margins entire, rounded base usually SUBSYMMETRIC (unusual for many sandmats), tip rounded or occasionally notched, glabrous. Usually only midvein conspicuous.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Distinct thin awl-shaped (subulate) glabrous scales, 0.5–0.7 mm, at leaf junctions. Distinguish from hairs under a strong lens; existing habit photograph cannot prove individual stipules.

key_traits.label: Cyathia
key_traits.text: Usually solitary at distal nodes on 0.3–0.7 mm stalks. Cup-like involucre 0.8–1.2 × 0.7–1 mm glabrous; 4 RED TO PURPLE slightly concave ELLIPTIC glands roughly 0.2–0.3 × 0.4–0.5 mm; appendages ABSENT. No white petal-like crescents expected.

key_traits.label: Capsules
key_traits.text: Broadly ovoid 3-lobed glabrous capsules 1.3–1.8 × 1.5–2 mm; this is compatible with golondrina and cannot resolve both species alone.

key_traits.label: Seeds
key_traits.text: WHITISH COAT OVER REDDISH-BROWN underneath; narrowly oblong, distinctly 4-angled, 1.5–2 × 1.3–1.8 mm, usually 5–7 FAINT shallow transverse ridges/wrinkles. E. theriaca var. theriaca commonly has smaller seeds with 2–4 PROMINENT transverse ridges. Mature seed macro with calibrated scale needed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Very tiny opposite nearly ROUND, entire-margined hairless leaves (1–3.2 mm long)

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Subsymmetrical rounded leaf bases unlike strongly oblique leaves of many Chamaesyce

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Cyathium at distal node, purple ELLIPTIC glands with NO white appendages

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Distinct thin 0.5–0.7 mm glabrous subulate stipules

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mature 1.5–2 mm 4-angled seed with 5–7 weak transverse ridges; essential for close E. theriaca comparison
